newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian directors see brighter outlook.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian directors see brighter outlook.

text.p: Australian company directors have become more optimistic about the outlook for the economy, company prospects and profitability, a survey released on Monday showed.
The survey of about 500 company directors by the Australian Institute of Company Directors (AICD) and KPMG found an overall strengthening in business confidence.
In the March quarter, 38 percent of directors surveyed expected the Australian economy to improve over the next six months, up from 29 percent in the December quarter.
The major shifts in perception came from the construction and utilities sector, reflecting the recovery in housing and construction, as well as the finance and manufacturing sectors.
Optimism about company prospects has remained fairly stable, but 57 percent of manufacturing industry directors were more optimistic compared with 38 percent in the December quarter.

KPMG executive director John Harkness said 54 percent of directors expected no change in interest rates, compared with 23 percent previously. "Directors no longer have strong expectations of further falls in interest rates," he said.
Harkness said 60 percent of directors expected no change in inflation, up from 46 percent in December, but 73 percent believe wage costs would continue to rise.
"These results suggest that directors perceive a scenario for business whereby wage growth demand will not translate into inflationary pressures," he said.
The percentage of companies expecting sales on budget rose from 39 percent to 45 percent, with the improvement coming from those who had expected sales below budget.
Directors expecting an improvement in sales next quarter, compared with the previous corresponding quarter, improved to 62 percent from 53 percent.
